by_judge.judge: S SUNIL DUTT YADAV & HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR

narrative:
On November 13, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 44.0%, resolving 1,165 cases out of 2,647 scheduled across 60 judges. This performance reflects an 8.0 percentage point increase in hearing efficiency compared to the previous day (36.0% on November 12, with 1,191 of 3,309 heard), aligning closely with the 44.8% rate recorded on November 11.

Bench efficiency varied considerably across court halls. The division bench of Jayant Banerji and N.V. Bhavani in Hall 3 maintained exceptional output, hearing 27 of 29 scheduled matters (93.1%). Among single-judge benches, V Srishananda (Hall 23) and Ravi V Hosmani (Hall 19) achieved high conversion rates of 81.5% (66 of 81) and 80.0% (44 of 55), respectively. In contrast, S Rachaiah (Hall 27) heard 3 of 42 cases (7.1%), while Shivashankar Amarannavar (Hall 22) heard zero of his 98 scheduled cases—a significant drop from his 96.9% hearing rate on November 12.

Procedural stage analysis reveals that Preliminary Hearings saw the highest clearance rate at 70.9% (214 of 302 heard). Matters listed under Orders reached a 48.2% conversion rate (356 of 738 heard), improving from 38.1% on November 12. Final Hearing matters recorded the lowest rate at 27.7% (119 of 429 heard), though this marked a clear improvement over November 12's 14.8% rate.

By case type, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest share of the docket, with 463 of 982 cases heard (47.1%), up from 35.1% on the previous day. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) recorded a 40.1% hearing rate (202 of 504), while Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) lagged at 30.5% (102 of 334). Specialized categories achieved high clearance, led by Civil Petitions (CP) at 82.5% (33 of 40) and Civil Contempt Petitions (CCC) at 81.1% (30 of 37).
